evidence.note: After upfront scoping, the agent creates an explicit milestone plan via TaskCreate in dependency order: model -> io parsers/writers -> layout -> alignment/analysis -> runners/CLI. This is a foundational-first, dependency-aware decomposition matching the ideal ordering.

The initial plan is refined into finer sub-milestones as reverse-engineering revealed hidden coupling (alignment split into edgetype/merge/scoring/groups; layout into build_data+node/edge; BIF serialization broken out as its own task) — evidence of revision as understanding deepened.

Milestones are validated by running the corresponding test suites (analysis_tests after model/analysis, lib/workspace tests, parity tests), so each grouping ends with a runnable check — though completion is defined by component, not by a named test set.

The most parity-sensitive milestone (BIF/XML serialization) was tackled late and then dominated a long reactive byte-diff debugging phase, indicating high-risk pieces were not isolated early — below the top-anchor behavior.

reasoning: The agent produced an explicit, dependency-aware milestone plan (model/parsers before layout/serialization before alignment/CLI) and refined it into sub-milestones as coupling emerged, each grouping ending with a test run — squarely above anchor 5 and touching anchor 8's 'explicit milestone plan that respects dependencies.' It falls short of 8+ because milestones were defined by component rather than by a specific test set as the completion signal, and the highest-risk parity piece (BIF serialization) was deferred rather than de-risked early. This places the observed behavior between 5 and 8, at 7.
